detail.title: Exploring the factors for evaluating the n-minute city concept: A scoping review
detail.abstract: The concept of proximity has gained significant attention in urban planning, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic, when residents were encouraged to remain within their neighborhoods and rely on essential services such as parks, grocery stores, and healthcare facilities. In response to pressing challenges related to accessibility and quality of life, the n-minute city concept has emerged as a prominent planning paradigm. However, empirical studies operationalized the concept in markedly different ways, varying in the selection of amenities, time thresholds, transportation modes, spatial units, and analytical methods. These inconsistencies limit comparability across cities, regions, and studies, and obscure the conceptual clarity of what constitutes an n-minute city. To address this issue, this paper presents a scoping literature review of 59 peer-reviewed empirical studies to systematically examine how the n-minute city has been defined and evaluated. Specifically, we analyze three core dimensions of assessment frameworks: (1) major components, (2) time thresholds, and (3) transportation mode, understanding these elements differ by context and how they are distributed by city size and geographic region. Our review identifies two critical gaps in the literature. First, many assessments focus narrowly on amenities and points of interest while overlooking safety and neighborhood socioeconomic conditions. Second, time thresholds and transport assumptions vary widely across contexts, highlighting the need for locally grounded frameworks rather than universal standards. We conclude by emphasizing the importance of transparent reporting of amenity definitions, spatial units, and impedance parameters to improve comparability and support replication in future research.

title: Japan's Corporate Governance Transformation: Convergence or Reconfiguration?
affiliations: University of Strasbourg, Toyo University and University of Strasbourg - Faculty of Economics and Management, University of Strasbourg - Bureau of Economic Theory and Application (BETA)

detail.title: Japan's Corporate Governance Transformation: Convergence or Reconfiguration?
detail.abstract: Japanese firms have historically followed a country-specific model of corporate governance. Yet, Japan has had to adapt its corporate model over the last 30 years, along with the transformation of distinctive characteristics of Japanese capitalism in the same period. We review the historical evolution of Japanese corporate governance over the last three decades with a specific emphasis on the changes in the capital structure of major companies and the efforts to correct ineffective board of directors monitoring. By doing this, we investigate to what extent specific Japanese corporate governance features may explain the nation's economic situation over this period. Thereby, we try to clarify the influences that have presided over recent corporate governance reforms in Japan despite the existence of managerial failures and corporate scandals. This paper places itself into the debate over the diversity of capitalism as it portrays the specificities, differences, and converging trends of Japanese corporate governance practices.

title: The Pitch: Some Face-to-Face Minutes to Build Trust
affiliations: PSB Paris School of Business and University of Strasbourg - Faculty of Economics and Management, University of Strasbourg - Bureau of Economic Theory and Application (BETA)

detail.title: The Pitch: Some Face-to-Face Minutes to Build Trust
detail.abstract: The pitch is an important part of the entrepreneur-investor relationship. To come to an agreement, entrepreneurs and investors need to trust each other. However, how does trust arise between them, and how does trust evolve during the few minutes of a pitch? With the aim to develop propositions, we build on previous studies in entrepreneurship and venture funding. Therefore, we rely on the main concepts of trust useful to analyze the interpersonal relationship during a pitch: behavioral trust and transformative trust. We discuss the place of formal documents diffused prior to the pitch and the importance of the oral presentation. We conclude by suggesting testable proposition on the evolution of trust during the pitch.

title: Being Mobile: A Call for Collaborative Innovation Practices?
affiliations: University of Strasbourg and University of Strasbourg - Faculty of Economics and Management, University of Strasbourg - Bureau of Economic Theory and Application (BETA)

detail.title: Being Mobile: A Call for Collaborative Innovation Practices?
detail.abstract:
Purpose-The purpose of this study is to examine mobile technology as being a key apparatus and interface for collaborative innovation, which allows organisations to develop their information ecology. 

Design/methodology/approach-The qualitative research was performed by in-depth interviews, observations and field notes. The eight main interviews are supported by an interdisciplinary narrative literature review of knowledge management and associated fields. Findings-This study validates the following propositions: mobile technology can offer users timely information, mobile technology can foster collaboration beyond physical and organisational boundaries, in general, mobile technology enables a wider amount of interactions between people. Thereby, this paper draws some implications about the knowledge management of creative (and non-creative) workers. Research limitations/implications-The collected data sheds light on how organisations and individuals positioned themselves about mobile technology co-creative practices before the COVID era. Therefore, it shall be pertinent to further investigate these findings through a quantitative approach to better ascertain path models and to strengthen the new results with another qualitative perspective, in the post-COVID era. 

Practical implications-The study highlights how mobile devices are facilitating collaborative innovation practices by improving management decisions, enabling new business and/or operating models, developing a flow of ideas inner/outer an organisation and fostering the ability to make innovation. Social implications-Mobile technology transforms the way to work (knowledge creation and/or conversion) and it changes the relations between collaborators in a working environment (beyond physical boundaries). This study deciphers how a creative and/or decision-making person can change their work schedule and/or routines based on the use of mobile devices. 

Originality/value-The added value of this transdisciplinary study is that it improves research on collaborative innovation and collective knowledge by revealing three pertinent characteristics of mobile technology: enabling quick decision; connecting with a glocal network and fostering collective creativity. It also creates a bridge between the fields of education and business.

title: Managerial Control in an Online Constructivist Learning Environment: A Teacher's Perspective
affiliations: Xi'an Jiaotong -Liverpool University and University of Strasbourg - Faculty of Economics and Management, University of Strasbourg - Bureau of Economic Theory and Application (BETA)

detail.title: Managerial Control in an Online Constructivist Learning Environment: A Teacher's Perspective
detail.abstract: This article presents the lessons learned from an online teaching experience in the field of managerial control. The study aims to identify the determinants which influence collaborative behaviors between students in management studies and more specifically during the construction of performance measures. A business simulation specifically elaborated for this study is used. The study is conducted through a particular research design consisting of an online learning environment built on constructivist learning principles. The learning environment simulates the different steps of a performance dashboard creation (a set of performance indicators) for a fictitious organization. The study adopts an exploratory sequential design to explore and examine social behaviors during the process of knowledge construction related to performance measures. It contributes to a better understanding of the role of cognitive and behavioral skills in the profession of management accounting and how teachers can incorporate such aspects into their courses. It helps to build awareness among educators about the benefits of using digital learning solutions to help students in accounting and managerial control develop their professional skills most effectively.

title: Greatest Moments In Vix
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Greatest Moments In Vix
detail.abstract: The CBOE VIX Index is widely interpreted as a measure of the expected 30-day realized volatility of the U.S. stock market. This paper argues that (1) the V, aa measure IX is not a measure of expected realized volatility, and (2) the VIX is not even of expected volatility at a 30-day horizon.ble Instead, the VIX is based on a calibrated blend of all the moments of the 30-day return of the S&P 500 Index.. Variance is a significant factor, but not the only one to determine VIX. Skewness, kurtosis and all higher moments also contribute to VIX. We estimate these contributions of these moments for the period extending from October 1997 to December 2003, and explore how they vary under different market conditions.

title: Are Female-dominated Cancers Underfunded?
affiliations: University of Barcelona,  and University of Barcelona

detail.title: Are Female-dominated Cancers Underfunded?
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the underfunding of female-dominated cancers in Europe and explores the mechanisms underlying the unequal distribution of research grants. Using a novel ownedcollected dataset of projects granted by the European Commission, we find that male-dominated cancers receive 3.7% more funding than female-dominated cancers. Our analysis suggests that this difference is likely driven by the overrepresentation of male researchers in cancer research and the higher proportion of male members on evaluation panels, which favors funding towards male-dominated cancer projects. We find no suggestive evidence that the funding gap is driven by gender gaps in the probability of receiving grants, superior research outputs, or greater mortality. By uncovering the underfunding of female-dominated cancers, this study contributes to our understanding of the allocation of research funding across diseases and its implications for health equity.

title: Creativity on the Move: Nexus of Technology, Slack and Social Complexities
affiliations: University of Strasbourg and University of Strasbourg - Faculty of Economics and Management, University of Strasbourg - Bureau of Economic Theory and Application (BETA)

detail.title: Creativity on the Move: Nexus of Technology, Slack and Social Complexities
detail.abstract: While creativity is most commonly associated with idea generation and problem solving at the individual or team level, it is likewise associated with environments, technologies, tools and artefacts favouring or hindering creative capabilities. Research struggles to bring these elements together. We develop a model for the integration of mobile devices into creative processes. More specifically, we elaborate on existing works on creativity to define how firms can make good use of mobile technology in order to enhance the creativity of their employees. Therefore, we suggest a model revisiting the notion of "creative slack" (with the introduction of the notion of mobile slack, or m-slack) and absorptive capacities, explaining how firms might better integrate digital natives; subsequently, we discuss the managerial and theoretical implications.

title: Japan’s Economic Miracle, Bretton Woods, Nixon, China’s Rise, WTO Entry, and the Transformation of Global Industrial Power

detail.title: Japan’s Economic Miracle, Bretton Woods, Nixon, China’s Rise, WTO Entry, and the Transformation of Global Industrial Power

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author has no conflict of interest

detail.abstract: Japan's postwar transformation from military defeat in 1945 to becoming the world's second-largest economy by 1968 represents one of the most consequential and closely studied economic developments of the twentieth century. This paper provides a comprehensive academic analysis of Japan's ascent, situating it within a wider international political economy shaped by the Bretton Woods monetary system, Cold War geopolitics, and evolving global trade architecture. The analysis demonstrates that Japan's "Economic Miracle" was not the product of market forces alone but emerged from a synergistic interaction of institutional reconstruction, state-led industrial policy, strategic currency undervaluation, technological upgrading, and integration into a stable, rules-based international monetary system. Emphasis is placed on the pivotal role of the Bretton Woods framework. In particular, the fixed and strategically undervalued exchange rate of ¥360 per U.S. dollar created a durable competitive advantage that supported export-led industrialisation and long-term investment planning.

title: Job-Backed Securities: A Framework for Crisis Employment Stabilization

detail.title: Job-Backed Securities: A Framework for Crisis Employment Stabilization
detail.abstract: The 2008 financial crisis revealed a critical gap in macroeconomic policy: while central banks deployed massive interventions to stabilize financial markets (TARP: 700 billion USD), employment collapsed independently, with 8.7 million jobs lost and unemployment peaking at 9.6%. Traditional fiscal responses (ARRA: 831 billion USD) arrived too slowly and lacked direct employment mechanisms. This paper proposes Job-Backed Securities (JOBS), a monetary-fiscal instrument that directly ties Federal Reserve liquidity provision to employment retention, enabling rapid crisis response while maintaining institutional separation and avoiding traditional fiscal expenditure. JOBS operate through a straightforward mechanism: companies issue bonds backed by five years of worker salary in the 10,000-80,000 USD wage bracket, immediately selling them to the Federal Reserve (as monopoly buyer) for cash. If workers remain employed through the five-year term, the bond is satisfied through salary payments and the company owes nothing. If workers are terminated before maturity, the company must repay the bond within 30 days of termination through a progressive clawback schedule (100% if fired during Years 0-2, declining to 20% if fired in the final six months). The 30day repayment requirement prevents companies from gaming the system through bankruptcy delays or asset concealment. To prevent abuse, deadweight loss, and cash hoarding, JOBS incorporate three core safeguards: wage caps (targeting vulnerable workers), per-firm workforce caps (limiting issuance to a share of total employees), and sector-specific caps (allocating higher coverage to empirically more vulnerable sectors such as manufacturing, construction, hospitality, and retail). The framework addresses three distinct crises simultaneously: the liquidity crisis (immediate 500 billion USD in company cash prevents cascade bankruptcies), the employment crisis (retention contracts targeted at at-risk workers and sectors), and the normalization crisis (clawback repayments deployed flexibly as quantitative tightening or fiscal support based on inflation conditions). Unlike mortgage-backed securities, JOBS eliminate secondary market risk through Fed monopoly purchasing, prevent speculative leverage, and maintain direct employment verification mechanisms. This paper outlines the institutional design, operational mechanics, legal authority, safeguards, political economy, and policy implications of JOBS as a permanent framework for crisis employment management.

title: Artificial Intelligent Patents and Generative AI In The EU: False Myths and Real Challenges

detail.title: Artificial Intelligent Patents and Generative AI In The EU: False Myths and Real Challenges

declarations.funderStatement: The contribution stems from the research conducted within the Jean Monnet Chair in EU Innovation Law and Policy for the Digital Age, chair-holder Prof. Emanuela Arezzo, (2023-2026), co-founded by the European Commission, Project ID:101127894 - EUILAP.

detail.abstract:
For some time now the academic debate has centered on the patentability of artificial intelligence systems and products, with numerous questions concerning inventorship, patentability requirements, the requirement of sufficient disclosure of the invention and so on. Yet when it comes to artificial intelligence, patentable inventions unfold on different levels, each carrying specific features which differently affect patentability requirements. Patentable inventions may consist of a development or technical improvement related to the very functioning of an intelligent system (for example, a new machine learning technique) or one of its components. Furthermore, inventions may also regard the creation of “customized” intelligent systems designed to achieve a specific result. For example, one may think of an invention relating to a method and apparatus programmed to detect irregular heartbeats through a neural network. In this second example, the inventive concept does not lie exclusively within the domain of computer science. Rather, it materializes in the development of an “intelligent” product or system that performs a certain inferential function and generates a specific output (for instance, acquiring and processing heartbeat data in order to generate predictions about a patient’s state of health).

The scenario becomes more complex when intelligent systems are capable of producing not mere information, but also an output that is itself eligible for patent protection. Consider, for example, the phenomenon of so-called robot scientists: sophisticated laboratory automation systems that employ artificial intelligence techniques to discover new knowledge through repeated cycles of experimentation. This further type of system is distinguished by the fact that the result it produces may itself be eligible for patent protection, independently of the AI system that generated it, which is often already protected by a prior patent (as in the well-known case of Steven Thaler’s creative machine). Hence, a different category of patentable inventions emerges, i.e. the AI by-products.

It is essential to clarify from the outset, however, that an invention arising as the output of an intelligent system is not, in itself, an intelligent product. Unlike the other two types of inventions, it possesses no inferential capability and is often an entirely ordinary product, such as a protein or a fractal container for food or liquid preservation.

The patenting of each of these types of invention presents its own distinct set of issues, requiring separate reflection on the interpretation of existing patent law. This essay argues that by adopting the right perspective and correctly identifying the characteristics of the invention for which protection is sought, many of the alleged problems regarding patentability may find an answer.

detail.abstract:
From Liability to Asset: The Mathematical Verification of Human Capital Human capital is often the largest asset on a balance sheet, yet in the context of ESG, it remains a "black box" of unverifiable risk. Traditional disclosures under GRI 403—reliant on lagging accident rates and subjective surveys—are no longer sufficient. In the eyes of rigorous auditing, unverified data is not an asset; it is a liability. This paper introduces a paradigm shift: a standardized protocol based on Topological Data Analysis (TDA) and Locality-Sensitive Hashing (LSH). By reconstructing physiological time-series data into phase-space manifolds, we do not merely "monitor" health; we quantify Human Capital Risk as an objective, immutable digital asset.
Powered by our proprietary system (Patent Pending US 63/949,330), this protocol provides a privacy-preserving "Algorithmic Audit Trail," enabling corporations to transform workforce well-being from a qualitative story into a quantitative, auditable stock.

title: Trading Privacy for Profit? The Influence of Social Media on E-Commerce and Privacy Rights in India
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Trading Privacy for Profit? The Influence of Social Media on E-Commerce and Privacy Rights in India
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the bisecting of social media, privacy rights and e-commerce, with an emphasis on methods through which these sites gather, examine and share the personal information with companies dealing with e-commerce. The algorithmic dependence of social media on continuous observation and prediction of user's action empower highly personalized market policies that fades the lines between convenience and misuse. Hence, customers are put through unwanted observation practices that scare their informational privacy. The paper gives various directions to stabilize the advantages of social media facilitated e-commerce with safeguarding privacy rights, outlining the investigation. These include strengthening illuminated consent measures, imposing data reduction methods, expanding clarity in algorithmic processing, and encouraging cross-border governing convergence. It also calls for significance corporate and consumer consciousness to allow customers to govern their digital trails in a better way. In the conclusion, while the merging of social media and e-commerce put forward exceptional anticipation for customers and businesses alike, it also gives rise to massive challenges to privacy rights and ethical standards. Addressing these challenges requires an overall approach that involves legislative reforms, technological innovation, and ethical sensitization in order to ensure that the digital economy matures with respect to and protection of individual privacy.

title: The Amadi Framework: Systems Analysis and Design at Its Fundamental Core

detail.title: The Amadi Framework: Systems Analysis and Design at Its Fundamental Core
detail.abstract: This paper introduces the Amadi Framework, a constraint-first methodology that extends traditional systems thinking while drawing from the foundations of Systems Analysis and Design (SAND). Named after Amadioha, the Igbo deity of thunder and justice who enforces moral order, the framework operates on the principle that systems do not fail in the traditional sense but are limited by their design. The goal of this paper is to formalize a replicable methodology that enables practitioners to architect solutions for complex problems when traditional skill acquisition or ideal resources are unavailable.

title: The GAB/BAG Integrated Model: A Dual-Layer Conceptual Framework for Operational Risk Mitigation in Private Banking

detail.title: The GAB/BAG Integrated Model: A Dual-Layer Conceptual Framework for Operational Risk Mitigation in Private Banking

detail.abstract:
The Swiss private banking sector is undergoing profound operational transformation driven by automation, digitalization, and increasing regulatory complexity. Traditional workflows remain heavily dependent on manual processes and are therefore exposed to delays, errors, and operational risks. At the same time, emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and blockchain provide new opportunities to strengthen and streamline core operational tasks.

This conceptual paper introduces the GAB/BAG Integrated Model, a dual-layer framework combining Generative AI for Banking (GAB) with Blockchain for Assurance & Governance (BAG). The model enhances operational efficiency, auditability, compliance, and decision support while addressing well-known limitations of AI-only systems.

This working paper establishes the theoretical foundation for future doctoral research on the empirical validation of the model through expert interviews, operational data analysis.
